Unique persistent identifier for a saved batch setup record. The same saved batch setup may be loaded multiple times using the same batch_uid.
Unique identifier for a specific loaded/runtime batch instance. A new batch_run_uid shall be generated each time a saved batch setup is loaded.

Human-readable runtime identifier displayed to users in the UI, audit trail, report selection table, and Batch Report. The Displayed Run Instance ID shall allow users to distinguish multiple executions of the same saved batch name.
Runtime Batch Instance / Runtime Batch Card

The active batch workflow instance created when a saved batch setup is loaded. The runtime instance/card tracks selected equipment, current batch status, timestamps, user actions, equipment claims, audit records, and reporting context.
A runtime workflow status used to identify whether a selected equipment item is loaded, officially claimed, or released for batch workflow/reporting purposes.

Equipment claim state indicating that the equipment was selected for a loaded runtime batch instance/card. LOADED means the equipment is associated with the loaded batch, but it has not yet been officially acquired by a started batch.

Equipment claim state indicating that the equipment has been officially acquired by the first runtime batch instance to start. CLAIMED equipment shall be treated as unavailable to other runtime batch instances until released.

Equipment claim state indicating that equipment is available for use by another runtime batch instance. Equipment shall transition to RELEASED on Complete, Abort, or Archive, as defined by the batch workflow.

The Main Overview Screen allows users to navigate to Charts, Alarms, Reports, Batch Setup / Batch Report Setup, Level 2 Screens, and Level 3 Screens after login. Where runtime batch functionality is enabled, the Main Overview Screen may display active runtime batch cards. Runtime batch card behavior is defined in Section 10.The main overview screen allows the users to gain access to the system. Users can gain access to the following areas once logged in: Charts, Alarms, Reports, Batch Report Setup, Level 2 Screens, Level 3 Screens.
Batch Setup / Batch Report SetupBatch Report Setup

This screen allows authorized users to configure batch/report setup records and create runtime batch instances from saved setups. Users may enter or select batch name, batch suite, equipment selections, batch age or report duration, and reporting configuration. The screen supports Save and Load actions. Save stores or updates a batch setup record. Load creates a runtime batch instance/card. Detailed runtime behavior is defined in Section 10.1.This screen allows users to configure the data to be included in the Batch Report by selecting which devices should be included in the report, as well as the batch age. Accessed by clicking “Setup” on any screen’s batch controls.

This screen shows a dynamic trend chart that can be populated with available system data points. Both historical and real-time data are available. Accessed by clicking “Charts.”This screen shows a dynamic trend chart which can be populated with any data points in the system - both historical and real-time data is available. Accessed by clicking “Charts”.

This screen shows system alarms based on configured filters. Alarms can be filtered by status, including Active, Inactive, Acknowledged, and Unacknowledged. Alarm actions such as acknowledge, shelve, un-shelve, and clear shall be available according to configured security permissions. Accessed by clicking “Alarms.”This screen shows all system alarms based on the configured filters. Alarms can be filtered between any combination of status’s - Active, Inactive, Acknowledged, & Unacknowledged. Alarms can be cleared, acknowledged, shelved, or un-shelved from this screen. Accessed by clicking “Alarms”.

This screen displays modular Batch Reports with alarms, events, and data trends containing Key CPPs for devices configured in the report. The Reports screen shall allow users to select reports by Batch Name and Run Instance and/or Displayed Run Instance ID. Reports can be exported in PDF format by clicking the cloud icon in the lower right corner. Detailed runtime reporting requirements are defined in Section 10.4.This screen displays a modular batch report with alarms, events, and data trends containing key CPP’s for any devices configured in the report. Reports can be exported in .PDF format by clicking the cloud icon in the lower right corner. Accessed by clicking “Reports”.

These screens display enabled equipment dynamically from the Ignition tag browser structure. Equipment shall be organized by suite, room, and functional area. Functional areas shall include UPSTREAM, DOWNSTREAM, and ANALYTICS, or equivalent approved project folder names. Key CPPs are displayed under each device. A chart icon appears next to each Key CPP; clicking the icon opens a pop-up window with a live trend of the data point. Equipment source and inventory requirements are defined in Section 10.5.These screens display the devices in each of the separate labs, separated by room number and modality – Upstream, Downstream, & Analytical. Key CPP’s critical process parameters which are determined by the customer are displayed under each device (commonly referred to as “Key CPP’s”). A chart icon appears next to each Key CPP – clicking the icon will open a pop-up window with a live trend of the data point. Accessed by clicking the corresponding room title.

This screen displays critical process parameters for a selected device. A chart icon appears next to each CPP; clicking the icon opens a pop-up window with a live trend of the data point. This screen is accessed by clicking a device image on the overview screen or Level 2 screens.This screen displays all critical process parameters for a given device. A chart icon appears next to each CPP – clicking the icon will open a pop-up window with a live trend of the data point. | This screen is accessed by clicking on any device image on the overview screen or level 2 screens.

The Equipment Tag Browser allows authenticated users to view equipment process-tag configuration from the live Ignition tag structure under [default]TBMC-SCADA/TW-LAB01. Authorized Supervisor users may stage and save approved configuration changes, including CPP assignment, OPC source path, historization, engineering limits, alarm enablement, and alarm delay. Saved changes write to live Ignition tag configuration after confirmation and are recorded through the Ignition audit system.
